key_insight: CREW replaces rigid, predefined multi-agent workflows for related work generation with autonomous reinforcement-learned coordination among LLM agents.
engineering_relevance: The framework suggests a more adaptable and cost-efficient way to automate literature synthesis for scientific writing pipelines.
method: Agents choose actions dynamically: Retrieve, Disseminate, Compose, and Critique.
Policy learning is optimized with Independent Proximal Policy Optimization (IPPO).
The design bypasses heuristic step-by-step pipelines in favor of collaborative decision-making.
evidence_signal: Experiments on a standard related work generation benchmark show strong quality gains over baselines while also lowering token cost.
watch_item: Performance depends on stable multi-agent RL training and benchmark transferability, so results may be sensitive to task setup and reward design.
paper_title: Assembling the CREW: A Collaborative Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Automated Related Work Generation
